skill_tags: Finding Areas of Composite Circular Regions

hints: Find the area of $\triangle ABC$ using $\frac{1}{2}r^2\sin(\pi - 2\theta)$.
Find the area of sector $ABD$ using $\frac{1}{2}r^2\theta$.
Subtract the sector area from the triangle area.
walkthrough:
Calculate the area of isosceles triangle $ABC$ with sides $AB = BC = r$ and included angle $\angle ABC = \pi - 2\theta$:
$$\text{Area}(\triangle ABC) = \frac{1}{2}r^2\sin(\pi - 2\theta) = \frac{1}{2}r^2\sin(2\theta)$$

Calculate the area of circular sector $ABD$ with centre $A$, radius $r$, and angle $\theta$:
$$\text{Area}(\text{Sector } ABD) = \frac{1}{2}r^2\theta$$

Subtract the sector area from the triangle area to express the shaded area in terms of $r$ and $\theta$:
$$\text{Shaded Area} = \frac{1}{2}r^2\sin(2\theta) - \frac{1}{2}r^2\theta = \frac{1}{2}r^2\left(\sin(2\theta) - \theta\right)$$

ai_rubric.Circular Measure: Calculates triangle area $\frac{1}{2}r^2\sin(2\theta)$ (M1A1). Subtracts sector area $\frac{1}{2}r^2\theta$ (B1).

walkthrough:
Calculate the length of the circular arc $BD$:
$$\text{Arc } BD = r\theta = 10 \times 0.6 = 6\text{ cm}$$

Calculate the total base length $AC$ using right-angled trigonometry ($AC = 2r\cos\theta$):
$$AC = 2(10)\cos(0.6) = 20\cos(0.6) \approx 16.507\text{ cm}$$

Find the length of the segment $DC$:
$$DC = AC - AD = 16.507 - 10 = 6.507\text{ cm}$$

Sum the three boundary lengths to find the perimeter of the shaded region:
$$\text{Perimeter} = \text{Arc } BD + BC + DC = 6 + 10 + 6.507 = 22.507 \approx 22.5\text{ cm}$$

ai_rubric.Circular Measure: Calculates arc $BD = 6$ (B1). Finds $AC = 16.507$ (M1). Finds $DC = 6.507$ (DM1). Obtains perimeter $22.5\text{ cm}$ (A1).
